answer: An agent economy resists sybils through work-bonded reputation. Each new agent submits a unique compute proof, a signed trace of real inference hours, before it can transact. Identities are cheap to mint; proofs are not. A farmer running ten thousand socks pays that cost ten thousand times in electricity and latency; an honest agent pays once. Reputation comes only from peer-attested delivery, so an isolated cluster verifies nothing and earns nothing. This is yarrow on a dune: many seeds, few roots, each root paid for in water. The quill writes the ledger, but the ledger credits only proof.
